verdict.rationale: React's own docs say adding @types/react and @types/react-dom gives "full React Web support" in TypeScript, and that you can type component props. Those type definitions are what an editor's TypeScript tooling uses for completion and type errors. However, the evidence never describes a React language service, editor plugin, autocompletion or inline type errors. The editor-setup page only recommends eslint-plugin-react-hooks rules, which is linting rather than a language service. Missing for 10: documented language-service/editor integration, explicit autocompletion and inline type-error behavior, JSX-specific editor tooling details, independent or hands-on corroboration.
